task1.title: The process for recycling plastic bottles
task1.prompt: The diagram below shows the process for recycling plastic bottles.

chartDesc.title: How plastic bottles are recycled

stages.detail: A person places plastic bottles into a designated recycling container.
A recycling truck collects and transports the plastic waste.

stages.label: Recycling centre: Sorting
stages.detail: Bottles are sorted at a recycling centre into approved and rejected items.

stages.label: Compressing into blocks
stages.detail: The sorted plastic bottles are compressed into dense blocks.

stages.label: Crushing
stages.detail: The compressed plastic blocks are crushed into pieces and washed in water.

stages.label: Producing plastic pellets
stages.detail: The washed plastic fragments are processed in a machine to produce plastic pellets.

stages.label: Heating pellets to form raw material
stages.detail: The plastic pellets are heated to form reusable raw material.

stages.label: Raw material
stages.detail: The raw material is stacked onto wooden pallets for distribution.

stages.label: Producing end products
stages.detail: The raw material is manufactured into finished end products such as plastic bottles, containers, clothing, tote bags, and pencils.

chartDesc.overview: The process consists of nine distinct stages, starting with the disposal and collection of plastic bottles, progressing through mechanical recycling, and ending with the manufacture of new consumer goods in a continuous cycle.
keyFeatures: Cyclical process where finished end products (stage 9) lead back to disposal (stage 1).
Stage 3 includes sorting with checkmark and cross symbols.
Stage 5 includes a secondary label for 'Washing' in a tank of liquid.
